D015-D007_h001.question:
It’s been a little over a year now that I’ve felt like this, and it just isn’t letting up. Most days I wake up with this heavy, bleak feeling, like there’s no point to anything. Even simple things, like doing laundry or answering emails, feel overwhelming.

My mind feels slow and foggy, like I’m moving through molasses. I reread the same paragraph over and over and it doesn’t stick. I’ve fallen behind in my program, and I barely go out or talk to classmates anymore.

Over the past few months, it’s gotten darker. I’ve been thinking a lot about ending things, not just vague thoughts—more like mapping out when I could do it so no one would find me in time, and what method would definitely work.

On top of that, I sometimes hear a man’s voice commenting on how “special” I am or how I’m meant for some big, important destiny, like I have some hidden power. I know it sounds bizarre, but in those moments it feels absolutely real. These voices and ideas only happen when I’m in this really low, depressed state—they’re not there when my mood lifts even a little.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h022.question:
I guess this really started about eight months ago. I used to love going into the shop early, picking out colors, making arrangements. Now it’s like there’s just…nothing inside. I don’t feel sad exactly, more like hollow, like I’m going through the motions on autopilot. Even when customers smile or my husband jokes with me, it doesn’t really touch me.

Nights are awful. I wake up 3–4 times from these really vivid nightmares—people I love dying, my flowers rotting, my own body falling apart. I wake up sweaty and terrified, and then I can’t get back to sleep. When I’m awake, I keep replaying the smallest things I’ve done wrong—snapping at a customer years ago, forgetting my sister’s birthday once—and I can spend hours just mentally beating myself up over it.

I’ve been eating a lot more, especially in the evenings, almost like I’m trying to fill that emptiness. I’ve gained weight, which just adds to the self‑loathing.

Lately I’ve become convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body—that my organs are decaying or infected—even though my doctor says all my tests are fine. Sometimes, especially when I’m feeling the most low, I hear this woman’s voice, very clear, telling me I’m disgusting, that I don’t deserve my husband, that I’m a burden. Those voices and the belief about my body only happen when I’m in this really dark, empty state; on the rare days I feel a bit lighter, they’re not there at all.

All of this has really affected my work—my arrangements look half‑hearted, I forget orders, and I’ve cut my hours because I just can’t keep up. My husband says I’m not myself anymore.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D015-D007_h022.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h023.question:
It’s been about eight months now where I just feel…hollow. Not even sad most of the time, more like numb inside. I go to the office, clean teeth, make small talk with patients, but it feels like I’m on autopilot. When I get home, I just zone out on the couch. I’ve cut my hours because I can’t keep up the pace.

Sleep is awful. I fall asleep okay, but then I’m up at 2 or 3 a.m., lying there for hours, mind spinning. I keep replaying tiny things I’ve done wrong—like snapping at a patient once, or forgetting to call my mom back—and I beat myself up over them nonstop. I can’t let any of it go.

I’ve put on a lot of weight these past months, more than ten pounds, mostly from late-night snacking because being awake feels unbearable.

Lately, I’m convinced my husband is cheating on me. I check his phone, watch how he talks to coworkers. There’s no real proof, but I can’t shake the belief. Sometimes I smell perfume in our bedroom when no one’s been there. Those thoughts and smells only started after this whole low period began, and they never happen outside of it.
D015-D007_h023.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D015-D007_h023.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h024.question:
For about eight months now, I’ve felt like I’ve just sunk into this hole I can’t get out of. It’s not just being sad — it’s this heavy, constant dread from the moment I wake up, when I can even get up. Most nights I sleep 10–12 hours and still feel exhausted, and on weekends I’ll just stay in bed half the day. I used to be very on top of things at work, but lately I struggle to get through basic emails, and my team has started taking over parts of my job.

I’m also eating much more than I used to, especially in the evenings — bread, snacks, anything — and I’ve gained weight, which makes me feel even worse. I can’t shake this belief that I somehow caused terrible things that have happened at work and in my family, like I’m cursed and everyone is suffering because of me, even when it doesn’t make any sense.

On top of that, I’m convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body, like my organs are rotting. Sometimes I smell this awful, rotten odor coming from myself that no one else seems to notice. Those smells and these fixed ideas only show up when I’m in this really low state — they’re tied to this depression, not separate from it.
D015-D007_h024.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D015-D007_h024.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h025.question:
I’ve just been…low for a long time now. It’s been at least eight months. I cry at the smallest things—commercials, kids getting on and off the bus, driving past the cemetery where my wife’s buried. I can’t seem to hold it in, even when I’m on my route, so I try to wipe my eyes before the kids see.

When I’m not driving, I’m in bed. I can sleep 12, 14 hours and still feel exhausted. On weekends I barely get up except to use the bathroom. Food doesn’t interest me anymore; I used to love big breakfasts at the diner, but now I pick at toast or just skip meals. I’ve lost weight without really trying.

I keep thinking my wife’s death was my fault, that God’s punishing me, and that I deserve every bad thing that happens. I obsess over tiny mistakes at work like they’re unforgivable.

Lately, when I’m really down, I feel like one of the younger teachers is secretly in love with me—like she’s sending me hidden messages. At the same time, I sometimes feel hands on my shoulders or something crawling on my skin when no one’s there. Those things only seem to happen when I’m at my worst mood-wise; when I’m having a slightly better day, they don’t happen. All of this is making it hard to keep doing my job.
D015-D007_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
